notes: the assistant keeps its place, and a long chat stops paying full price for what it already said. Work of more than a few steps now starts with a task list it writes and keeps up to date: it shows as a card in the conversation and as a strip over the message box saying how far along it is and which step is open. It survives a reload and is re-sent every turn, so neither compaction nor shortened tool results can make it lose the thread. When a turn runs out of tool calls the reply ends with a Continue button that picks up the steps that are left, instead of leaving you to describe where it stopped. Sub-agents can fan out: several independent jobs go in one run_subagent call and run at the same time, so three sweeps of a repository cost one wait rather than three, and Settings → Model can point them at a smaller model — exploring is mostly reading — with their tokens billed to the chat at that model's price. Reasoning effort is finally a setting, minimal to high, shown next to the model name and never spent on auto-titling or compaction. And the request itself is now built to be cached: what changes between turns — the open folder, the git state, the date — has moved out of the system prompt and travels with the message it belongs to, so everything in front of it is identical from one turn to the next, with explicit cache markers for the models that cache nothing without them. Settings → Model says whether hits are actually coming back, because a proxy that drops the marker looks exactly like one that honours it. Fixed: opening a chat on a folder the browser had not granted could reload AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md in a loop until the tab died
